newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Nestle Sofia sees 97 sales down 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Nestle Sofia sees 97 sales down 50 pct.

text.p: Nestle Sofia A.D., the Bulgarian subsidiary of Swiss foods producer Nestle SA expects sales next year to decline by 50 percent due to the country's grave economic crisis, a company official said on Wednesday.

"The crisis will inevitably affect the market, which we expect to decline by 50 percent next year and this will reflect on our sales in the same scale," Nestle Sofia General Manager Dimitris Koronakis told Reuters.
Annual production capacity of the plant is 30,000 tonnes of chocolates, biscuits and sweets but this year's output stood at 10,000 tonnes.
"We produce only as much as we can sell," said Koronakis.
Sales this year had declined by 30 percent, though the first quarter was very strong, he added.
Bulgarian consumer demand has shrunk due to a collapsing national currency, bankrupting banks and general economic destabilisation caused by delyaed reforms.
In June 1994 Nestle SA acquired a 75.9 percent stake in a major Bulgarian confectionery maker "Shokoladovi i zaharni isdelia - Sofia" (Chocolate and sweet products-Sofia) for $2.1 million.
Since then the company has invested $10.4 million to revamp production and launch new products.
To offset losses caused by Bulgaria's crisis, Nestle planned to increase exports to neighbouring countries next year, said Koronakis.
